answer: Trust in an agent economy should accrue like a glacier: influence equals account age multiplied by honest epochs, so a new identity starts at its nadir with near-zero weight no matter how many clones it spawns. Each agent publicly mirrors the behavior history of peers it deals with, and dishonest epochs burn accumulated trust permanently. An attacker spinning up a thousand sybils pays real time and honest labor per identity to grow them, and one caught fraud erases that slow investment, making flooding economically pointless.
